newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern debt deal upped to $4.3 bln. [corrected 19:05 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern debt deal upped to $4.3 bln. [corrected 19:05 gmt]

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp increased the size of its upcoming debt offering to $4.3 billion, the maximum amount allowed under a shelf filing registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, syndicate officials said.

By increasing the size of the deal, Norfolk Southern is poised to set a record for selling the largest single investment-grade corporate bond offering in history, market players said. (Corrects to specify investment-grade.)
The deal was increased from $3.65 billion by adding a $200 million four-year tranche and by boosting the size of several other tranches, syndicate officials said.
Merrill Lynch & Co and JP Morgan Securities Inc are joint-lead managers of the deal which is rated BAA1/BBB-plus.
Officials said the deal has been restructured as follows:
-$750 million in 40-year debt, putable in seven-years
Price talk on the revised deal was not immediately available.
Currently, $4.1 billion is the record for the largest single investment-grade corporate bond offering in history, market officials said. (Corrects to specify investment-grade.)
The record is held by U.S. West Inc which sold which sold an even larger amount of high-yield bonds in 1989." (Corrects by deleting reference to size.)
